strengths: Addresses an important practical problem: preemptively estimating pretext task suitability without expensive full training, with significant computational savings (~50x speedup)

Well-motivated theoretical framework with clear derivation of three-factor decomposition (learnability, reliability, completeness) connecting traditional knowledge-integrated learning to semi/self-supervised learning

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including 115 pretext task variants, extensive robustness testing (algorithms, models, data distributions, hyperparameters), and proper statistical validation at 99% confidence level
Strong correlations on standard benchmarks (CIFAR-10: 0.785-0.820, CIFAR-100: 0.905-0.950) with well-designed ablation studies demonstrating necessity of all three metrics
Clear presentation with good visual communication and practical efficiency demonstration
weaknesses: Severely limited scope of evaluation: the 115 'different' pretext tasks are variants of a single task class (augmentation-based label invariance); no evaluation on fundamentally different pretext tasks (rotation prediction, jigsaw puzzles, masked image modeling), limiting generalizability claims

Critical methodological issue with reliability estimation: relies on surrogate oracle f̂_target trained on only 50 labeled samples, with no analysis of how surrogate errors propagate to reliability estimates; using an unreliable model to estimate reliability creates circular reasoning

Variable and unexplained performance degradation: ImageNet-200 results (0.675-0.678) are significantly lower than CIFAR; ResNet-50 semi-supervised achieves only 0.478; some algorithms (MoCo: 0.453, SimCLR: 0.557) show poor correlations—but the paper provides no principled analysis of when/why the method fails

Gap between theory and practice: Equation 8 provides an upper bound but tightness is never analyzed; no justification for why empirical estimates should satisfy theoretical bounds; no error propagation analysis for how estimation errors affect the final bound
Completeness estimation depends on heuristic prototype-matching with Euclidean distance in embedding space, which lacks justification and may not generalize across task types, models, or domains

Missing baselines and comparisons: no alternative methods compared; no simple baselines (e.g., learnability-only); only ablation studies provided; no comparison with brief training or other task selection approaches

Insufficient failure analysis and design justification: no explanation of outliers; why prototype-based prediction instead of direct predictions; why this data filtering strategy instead of cross-validation; what explains the polarized performance
